question: After all tested Dusk Facet-chip variants and the cross-enemy topology family are closed, does exact current-main expose one untested discrete enemy-Ward transition at the existing Attack damage seam?
scientificBasis: Exact hit_enemy algebra partitions every resolved Attack against a living enemy by pre-hit Ward, post-hit Ward and HP loss. The five frozen cells are exhaustive and mutually exclusive. Current Facet logic already recognises both cells with positive HP loss. The only uncovered discrete transition is positive Ward becoming zero with zero HP loss; rewarding retained Ward or a zero-damage no-Ward state would require a scalar threshold rather than a state transition.

frontierScope.included: One deterministic boolean mapping at hit_enemy after final Attack damage, enemy Ward absorption and HP loss are known. It may only turn the existing per-target pending-chip hit flag on when positive pre-hit enemy Ward becomes exactly zero without HP loss.
excluded: additional chip when HP loss already activates the existing hit flag

attackOutcomePartition.currentMapping: No chip and no enemy Ward transition.

selectedPrimitive.stateRepresentation: Existing local values blocked, e.block and loss after hit_enemy resolves final Attack damage.
selectedPrimitive.exactEffect: For Duskblade only, an Attack that absorbs positive enemy Ward to exactly zero while dealing zero HP loss sets the existing per-card, per-target pending-chip hit flag true. It awards the same one implicit Facet chip already used by blood; it never adds a second chip when loss is positive.
selectedPrimitive.multiHitSafety: The existing boolean hit flag collapses multiple hits. Later blood or another hit cannot stack this primitive within the same card and target.
